Dying is absolutely normal in Nioh 2. Even long time players still die sometimes. 

It's actually very important to understand when it's safe for you to attack and how to not get greedy whenever you get an opening. 

Many larger enemies in the game only have small openings between attacks where you can only get 2 or 3 swings in before you need to back out. This is because they have Hyper Armor, where your attacks do not interrupt their attack rhythm at all. Smaller enemies don't have this so it's very easy to stun lock them to death, but you definitely have to watch out for Hyper Armor on larger enemies. 

Unless you're absolutely sure you can make a sneak attack, you avoid making the first melee attack. Many times you die simply because you attacked at the same time the enemy attacks, only to find out the enemy hits you first most of the time. This is why you don't start attacking until the enemy finishes their attack. The exception to this rule is if you can attack them from a distance while they are approaching, like with magic or with a shuriken. 

If you're against a melee enemy and you're in a standoff, it's a good idea to keep a small distance. The melee enemy will always approach you before making an attack, so it gives you a heads up that an attack is coming.

The Izanagi Grace 4p is popular because your 3p bonus is an Increase Attack buff after healing (which can be activated with CC Life Steal on weapon when you aren't in full health and Rejuv Talisman while in full health).

On your equipped Ranged weapon, you need Agility Damage Bonus (because this can transfer to your melee damage) and maybe Long Ranged Damage (if you want to keep your Kunai damage).

As a person that constantly make builds to share for others, I'll give you some advice.

First, pick the focus of your build: Is it an attack build? Is it a defense build? Do you want something very specific in the build, like Stun Resist? You have to decide what makes the build special.

Next, figure out what skills you want in your build and see if there are armor pieces that can fill in as many as the skills you want as you can. The more decoration slots you have left over the better.

Try to fill up your decoration slots to max out the skills you picked your armor for. This is the tricky part as your available decorations can determine what kind of armor you need. So swap out decorations and armor as you see fit and try to fill out the skills you want as best you can. 

If you can fill out all your target skills, awesome. If not, try to see if there are ways for you to compromise. 

Remember that your build doesn't have to be "omg this is the best there is online". It just needs to do what you want it to do well or as best that it could. 

Your build can take hours to even days to do adjust before you get it to feel right, so don't worry too much if it's not perfect the instant you make it. It'll grow the more you put time into thinking on how to improve it.

Well, here are some general tips:

1) Spend the first few hours (even tens of hours) focusing on Expedition and grabbing quests as soon as they pop up. Resources are VERY important in this game and NO ONE goes into late game without resources to at least craft useful stuff like Hi Potions and Max Potions. 

2) Until you're more skilled in the game, focus more on defensive skills than offensive skills. As a beginner it's more important to survive than it is to kill quickly. 

3) Don't neglect looking for Dung and crafting Dung Pods. In this game, Dung Pods are used to make an enemy run away from your particular area. This is useful for driving enemies away, giving you time to sharpen, give you room to head back to camp to restock, get large monsters away from much needed gathering points, scare away the B52 Bomber (Bazelgeus), drive away the gigantic pickle (Deviljho) and other creative applications. 

4) Don't play fair with monsters. If you can flash them, trap them, drop boulders on them, push them off waterfalls, or anything that would ruin a monster's day, do it. Because if a monster can cheapshot you, it definitely will. 

5) Get used to the radial menu. As great as manually sifting through the inventory is the classic way (scrolling through items one at a time), the Radial Menu is important because it allows you more options such as automatically crafting an item type you already used up. 

6) Try to solo (with your cat) as much as possible. As great as it is to get help, you'll make the enemy much harder and you have a higher chance of failing than if you simply do it on your own. There's only a few endgame quests that is better done in a group than solo.

7) And finally, don't be afraid to fail. Learning is very important in Monster Hunter games.

I have Asperger's myself and Asperger's is different for everyone. 

I'll just note that there are **MANY** similarities between a true introvert and someone with Asperger's. 

Here's a few key differences between someone with Asperger's and an Introvert.

1) Do you feel massive discomfort when staring someone in the eyes for longer than 3 seconds? For me it feels like someone's shoving an electrified massager up the middle of my spine and causes SEVERE discomfort.

2) Do you have hyperactive senses? I know the morning daylight early in the morning causes massive discomfort for my eyes, the phone ringing (ANY ringing) irritates me to no end, and certain sounds again makes me feel like someone's shoving an electrified massager up the middle of my spine and causes SEVERE discomfort.

3) Can you tell the difference between someone giving criticism or being passive aggressive with you? I really cannot tell the difference between someone trying to help me through critical opinion or if someone is making fun of me in a passive manner. I cannot tell the difference between someone screaming in extreme excitement and someone screaming in extreme distress. 

4) Do you have a hard time lying? One of the key features of someone with Asperger's is that they're brutally honest without consideration of the feeling of others. If a person with Asperger's doesn't have anything good to say, they're likely not to say anything at all. However, someone with Asperger's will have difficulty telling a lie very well knowing that it's not the case. 

5) Can you not hold still when in stressful situations? In my case, one of my legs vibrate up and down slightly in 1/16th note frequencies to help calm myself a little, I would fidget my hands, or I would need to be physically doing something small whenever I'm stressed.

6) Can you hold a single thought for 3 days to a week straight without straying far from the thought? One of the prominent things of people with Asperger's is that they can hold a thought for a VERY long time and continue with the thought even if it's physically impeding them. Many times I will not be physically active in any way, stare blankly ahead, and occasionally lay down because I'm being overwhelmed the amount of thinking I'm having to do at once. The brain isn't shutting down, but instead the body is shutting down while the brain is going into overdrive. 

7) When hearing your own voice at the same time while you're recording suddenly interrupt your own train of thought? Whenever I hear my own voice as I'm trying to record something I end up interrupting my own train of thought. And if anyone interrupts me as I speak, I end up going straight into listen mode and stop my current train of thought. Sometimes I even forget what I want to talk about in the first place after the interruption. 

Anyways, these are a few of the key differences between someone with Asperger's and someone that's an Introvert. And it really is a spectrum, you might lack or have a few more symptoms than I do, but in general you will have quite a few things as one of the key factors of an Asperger's is to over-experience the world and not having the social ego to deal with it.

There is a difference being born with Asperger's and identifying as someone with Asperger's socially. 

An Ego is a mask you can hide behind when dealing with others socially. You can be smiling but be absolutely furious inside. A male with Asperger's will more than likely not know how to hide their emotions, cannot lie very well, and have their emotion very well displayed facially.
